FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Sewing Machines Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1959 and was subsequently revised in 1967 and 1974. This third revision incorporates a number of changes which were felt necessary as a result of experience gained in the manufacture and use of presser bar and other developments in this field. The main modifications are: a) Deletion of hardness clause, b) Incorporation of geometrical tolerances in figure itself. In the preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from JIS B9028-1980 'Presser bar of sewing machine for house use' issued by Japanese Industrial Standards Committee. This edition 4.1 incorporates Amendment No. 1 (June 1996). Side bar indicates modification of the text as the result of incorporation of the amendment. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 1297 : 1991

Indian Standard HOUSEHOLD SEWING MACHINES PRESSER BAR -- SPECIFICATION ( Third Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard covers the requirements for pressor bars for sewing machines for household purposes. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed below are necessary adjuncts to this standard: IS No. Title Electroplated coatings of 1068 : 1993 nickel plus chromium and copper plus nickel plus chromium -- Specification ( third revision) 1570 (Part 3) : 1979 Schedules for wrought steels: Part 3 Carbon and carbon-manganese free cutting steels ( first revision ) 2102 (Part 1) : 1993 General tolerances Part 1 Tolerances for linear and angular dimensions without individual tolerance indications ( third revision ) inspection 2500 (Part 1) : 1992 Sampling procedures: Part 1 Attribute sampling plans indexed by acceptable quality level (AQL) for lot by-lot inspection (second revision) Methods for random 4905 : 1968 sampling 3 NOMENCLATURE The nomenclature of the pressor bar shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 4 MATERIAL Presser bars shall be manufactured from Free Cutting Steel such as 14C14S14 of IS 1570 (Part 3) : 1979. 5 DIMENSIONS The dimensions of the presser bar shall be as given in Fig. 2. 6 TOLERANCES 6.1 The tolerances shall be as shown in Fig. 2. 6.2 Tolerances on untoleranced dimensions shall be in accordance with medium class of IS 2102 (Part 1) : 1993. 7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 7.1 The outer diameter of the presser bars shall be precision ground. 7.2 The flat face and inclined faces of the presser bar coming in contact with the presser foot shall be machined to a fine finish. 7.3 The head of the presser bar shall be finished smooth and polished. 7.4 The two corner edges along the length of flat face shall be rounded off to ensure proper fitting of presser foot assembly. 7.5 The presser bar shall be had chrome plated with a minimum thickness of plating of 0.004 mm ( see IS 1068 : 1993 ).

8 SAMPLING Unless otherwise agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser, the sampling plan as given in Annex A shall be followed. For further information reference may be made to IS 2500 (Part 1) : 1992. 9 MARKING The presser bar may be marked with indication

of the source of manufacture. 10 PACKING Each presser bar shall be given a suitable anti-rust coating and securely packed in strong cardboard cartons in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each carton shall bear the manufacturer's name or trade-mark, the type and the description of the contents.

ANNEX A
( Clause 8 ) SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY A-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING A-1.1 Lot In any consignment, all the presser bars of the same type and manufactured from the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of presser bars to be selected at random for this purpose shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 2 Table 1 Scale of Sampling and Permissible Number of Defectives ( Clauses A-1.2, A-1.4 and A-2 )
No. of Presser Bars in the Lot For Dimensions, Tolerances and Workmanship and Finish Sample Size n (2) 5 8 13 20 32 50 80 125 Permissible No of Defectives1 (3) 0 0 0 1 1 2 3 5

N (1) Up to 15 16 to 40 41 to 110 111 to 300 301 to 500 501 to 800 801 to 1 000 1 001 and above

1 This ensures that lots containing only one and a half percent or less defectives will be accepted most of the times.

IS 1297 : 1991
A-1.3 If the presser bars are packed individually, in order to ensure randomness of selection, IS 4905 : 1968 shall be used. A-1.4 If the presser bars are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons (not less than 20 percent of the total in the lot subject to a minimum of 2) shall be chosen at random. From each of the cartons so chosen, an approximately equal number of presser bars shall be picked up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of presser bars specified in col 2 of Table 1. A 2 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY The presser bars selected according to A-1.2 and A-1.3 or A-1.4 shall be examined for dimensions (see 5), tolerances (see 6 ) and workmanship and finish (see 7 ). If the number of presser bars failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in col 3 of Table 1, the lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of these characteristics.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of BIS Catalogue and Standards : Monthly Additions'.
